mods.name: Keybinds Galore
mods.description:
Resolves Minecraft keybind conflicts instead of letting actions silently override each other. When two actions share a key, a selection menu opens so you pick the one you meant, every time.

Includes a pie menu and a list menu, a priority system for keys that should never ask, K-key priority capture, live conflict detection across categories, and an in-game config screen.

releases.notes:
KeybindsGalore 1.8.0 for Minecraft 26.3 on NeoForge

The NeoForge build for Minecraft 26.3. Same mod as the Fabric 26.3 build, on the NeoForge loader.

Nothing about the mod's behaviour changed. The pie menu, the list menu, the priority system, K-key priority capture, live conflict re-scanning, per-category filters, and the config screen all work exactly as they do on the Fabric build. The version number is unchanged, because this adds a loader rather than features.

## Requirements

- Minecraft 26.3
- NeoForge 26.3.0.26-beta or newer
- Java 25 or newer
- Cloth Config 26.3.159 or newer

No Fabric Loader, no Fabric API, and no ModMenu. The config screen is contributed through NeoForge's own settings extension point and appears in the mod list.

Note that NeoForge publishes 26.3 only as a beta at the time of writing, so this build tracks a moving target.

## What this port needed

Less than a port from an older Minecraft version, because the 26.3 Fabric build had already done the hard part. The engine work was already done and carried over unchanged:

- the client is on SDL3, so key handling uses `InputConstants.Type.KEYBOARD` with SDL scancodes
- rendering uses the `com.mojang.renderpearl` pipeline API
- `RingRenderer` needed no changes at all

Only the loader surface changed:

- the mod entrypoint is a NeoForge `@Mod(dist = CLIENT)` class
- key registration uses `RegisterKeyMappingsEvent`
- tick and connection events use the NeoForge equivalents
- the config directory uses `FMLPaths.CONFIGDIR`
- the ModMenu settings entrypoint became a `ModContainer` extension point, and `ModMenuIntegration` was removed, since NeoForge allows one `@Mod` class per mod id
- configuration loading moved to the first client tick, because `Minecraft.options` is still null during NeoForge mod construction
- `fabric.mod.json` is replaced by `META-INF/neoforge.mods.toml`

## Known issue

One harmless deprecation warning appears at startup. It comes from Cloth Config 26.3.159 itself, is upstream, and will disappear when Cloth ships a patch. Nothing in this mod causes it.

The limitations of the Fabric 1.8.0 build still apply, notably: no keyboard navigation in the pie menu, overlapping labels for long action names, and no detection of bindings another mod changes at runtime.

## Credits

Original project and original author: Cael. KeybindsGalore Plus: AV306. 1.20.x, 1.21.x and 26.x updates and re-writes: HVB007, plus the contributors listed in the mod metadata.

releases.notes:
KeybindsGalore 1.9.0+26.3 — Minecraft 26.3 (Fabric)

A port to Minecraft 26.3, which was not a content-only update.

Two platform changes broke the mod, both found by inspecting the 26.3 jar rather than the
changelog. If you maintain an addon that depends on this mod's internals, read the Removed
section.

## Changed

### GLFW was replaced with SDL3

Minecraft 26.3 dropped LWJGL's GLFW bindings and moved to SDL3, so key codes are now SDL
scancodes rather than GLFW keycodes.

- `InputConstants.Type.KEYSYM` was renamed to `InputConstants.Type.KEYBOARD`
- Unbound keys are now identified by a negative value, replacing `GLFW.GLFW_KEY_UNKNOWN`
- The default capture hotkey changed from the GLFW keycode for K to the SDL scancode for K

**Modders who read raw key values need to update.** Anything comparing against GLFW constants
will silently stop working.

### The GUI render pipeline moved packages

`RenderPipeline` is now `com.mojang.renderpearl.api.pipeline.RenderPipeline`. Mods that
implement a custom GUI element render state will need the same import change. `RenderPipelines.GUI`
is unchanged.

### Verified as unchanged

`KeyMapping.set`, `KeyMapping.click`, `KeyMapping.setDown`, the private `key`, `isDown` and
`clickCount` fields, `KeyMapping.Category.id()` and `.label()`, and `KeyEvent` /
`MouseButtonEvent` are all still present with the same shape. The selector release path and
all mixins are therefore unaffected.

## Requirements

- Minecraft 26.3
- Fabric Loader 0.19.3+
- Fabric API 0.161.0+26.3+
- Java 25+
- Cloth Config 26.3.159+
- ModMenu 21.0.0+ (optional, only for the settings screen)

Client-side only.

## Unverified

This port was confirmed to compile, to pass all 45 unit tests, and to launch with all mixins
applying and the startup conflict scan running. The user has played it briefly and reports it
works.

Not yet re-verified: the full manual test matrix, and pie visual fidelity. One specific item to
check is the `K` capture hotkey, whose SDL scancode was derived rather than read from vanilla
source, because letter keys have no named constant on `InputConstants`. If `K` does not open
the capture screen, rebind it in the vanilla Controls screen.

The carried-over known limitations from 1.8.0 still apply: no keyboard navigation in the pie
menu, possible label overlap, hex colour fields rather than pickers, and no detection of
runtime rebinds from other mods.

## Credits

Original project and original author: Cael. KeybindsGalore Plus: AV306. 1.20.x, 1.21.x and
26.x updates and re-writes: HVB007, plus the contributors listed in the mod metadata.

releases.notes:
KeybindsGalore 1.8.0+26.2-neoforge — Minecraft 26.2 (NeoForge)

First NeoForge release. This is the same mod as the Fabric `1.8.0+26.2` build, ported to
NeoForge. Behaviour is unchanged: the pie menu, the list menu, the priority system, K-key
priority capture, live conflict re-scanning, per-category filters, and the in-game config
screen all work the same way.

The Fabric edition is published separately as `1.8.0+26.2` and keeps its own version number.
The two are maintained on separate branches and versioned independently.

## Requirements

- Minecraft 26.2
- NeoForge 26.2.0.88 or newer
- Java 25+
- Cloth Config 26.2.155+

No Fabric Loader, no Fabric API, and no ModMenu. The config screen is contributed through
NeoForge's own settings extension point and appears in the Mods list.

Client-side only.

## What changed from the Fabric build

Only the loader-facing surface. The conflict engine, configuration model, and both selector
screens are untouched, because nearly all of the mod is plain Minecraft or plain Java.

- `ClientModInitializer` became an `@Mod(dist = CLIENT)` constructor
- Key registration moved to `RegisterKeyMappingsEvent`
- Tick and connection events moved to the NeoForge equivalents
- The config directory moved to `FMLPaths.CONFIGDIR`
- The ModMenu settings entrypoint became a `ModContainer` extension point
- Configuration loading moved to the first client tick, since `Minecraft.options` is still null
  during NeoForge mod construction
- The deprecation warning at startup is gone; `logoFile` is now `iconFile`

The mod now reports `1.8.0+26.2-neoforge` in-game.

## Known issues

One harmless deprecation warning appears at startup, from Cloth Config 26.2.155 itself. It is
upstream, inside that jar, and is already fixed in Cloth Config 26.3.159. It will disappear
when Cloth ships a 26.2 patch. Nothing in this mod causes it.

The limitations of the 1.8.0+26.2 Fabric build still apply, notably: no keyboard navigation in
the pie menu, overlapping labels for long action names, and no detection of bindings another
mod changes at runtime.

## Credits

Original project and original author: Cael. KeybindsGalore Plus: AV306. 1.20.x, 1.21.x and
26.x updates and re-writes: HVB007, plus the contributors listed in the mod metadata.

mods.name: Keybinds Galore
mods.description:
Resolves Minecraft keybind conflicts instead of letting actions silently override each other. When two actions share a key, a selection menu opens so you pick the one you meant, every time.

Includes a pie menu and a list menu, a priority system for keys that should never ask, K-key priority capture, live conflict detection across categories, and an in-game config screen.

1.8.0 for Minecraft 26.2 (Fabric). The config screen now works on 26.2, which was a known issue in 1.7.2.

releases.notes:
KeybindsGalore 1.8.0+26.2 — Minecraft 26.2 (Fabric)

The config screen now works on 26.2.

The previous 26.2 build shipped with a known issue: the ModMenu config screen failed, because
the Cloth Config release available at the time referenced a Minecraft class that no longer
exists. If you were told to edit `keybindsgalore.properties` by hand, you no longer need to.

Beyond that, conflict detection was rebuilt around a single canonical index, and the pie menu
was substantially reworked.

## Fixed

- Rebuilt conflict detection around one canonical index, instead of scattered callers.
- Conflicts now re-scan on startup, on joining a world, when the vanilla Controls screen
  closes, when config is saved, and when priorities change. A rebind done outside those moments
  could previously go unnoticed.
- The `K` capture key opens reliably. A direct edge-triggered path now runs alongside the
  previous poll-based one, so the first press is no longer sometimes swallowed.
- Pie menu labels are positioned radially and clamped to the screen. A label on a bottom wedge
  was previously pushed upward into the pie.
- Pie smoothness now divides its vertex budget across the wedges, so lowering the vertex count
  degrades the whole pie evenly instead of only making the cancel circle faceted.

## Added

- **Sector gradation** with a gradient intensity slider. Each wedge shades from a lighter inner
  edge to its outer colour.
- **Open animation** with a duration slider, 0 to 1000 ms. Set it to 0 for an instant menu.
  Labels appear once it finishes, because fading them in with it looked wrong.
- **Darken strength** slider for the pie menu background.
- **Selected sector expansion** now applies when you hover a wedge, defaulting to a subtle 0.06.
- **Label text shadow** follows its setting instead of being permanently on.
- **A separate list menu settings tab.** The list menu's colours and opacity were in the pie
  tab, where they had no effect and looked broken.
- Public API for other mods to register their actions, versioned via `ApiVersion`.

## Changed

- Config is read and written through a validated snapshot with atomic file replacement, instead
  of reflection over static fields.
- Colours use a real colour field with an alpha channel. Bounded numbers use sliders.
- Retired keys are stripped from existing config files on load, so upgrading no longer produces
  "no matching config field" errors.

## Removed

Nine configuration options were retired because they were unread, redundant, or 1.21.x
leftovers. Each is listed in `keybindsgalore.properties` with its replacement, and old values
are cleaned up automatically:

`PIE_MENU_COLOR_LIGHTEN_FACTOR`, `PIE_MENU_SELECT_COLOR`, `PIE_MENU_BLEND`,
`LABEL_TEXT_INSET`, `IGNORED_KEYS`, `INVERT_IGNORED_KEYS_LIST`,
`USE_SOFTWARE_RENDERING`, `LAZY_CONFLICT_CHECK`, `USE_KEYBIND_FIX`

`FILTERED_CATEGORY_KEYS` now defaults to empty. The old default was `Debug`, which does not
match any category in 26.2 and therefore did nothing.

## Requirements

- Minecraft 26.2
- Fabric Loader 0.19.3+
- Fabric API 0.152.1+26.2+
- Java 25+
- Cloth Config 26.2.155+
- ModMenu 20.0.2+ (optional, only for the settings screen)

Client-side only.

## Known limitations

- The pie menu has no keyboard navigation, which is the largest accessibility gap.
- Neighbouring wedge labels can overlap when action names are long. Labels are clamped so they
  are never cut off by the screen edge, but they cannot reflow.
- The pie menu does not pause the game, intentionally.
- Colour inputs are hex text fields, not RGB pickers. The Cloth Config release in use provides no
  picker widget.
- Bindings changed by another mod at runtime are not detected. Only the listed triggers cause a
  rescan.

## Credits

Original project and original author: Cael. KeybindsGalore Plus: AV306. 1.20.x, 1.21.x and
26.x updates and re-writes: HVB007, plus the contributors listed in the mod metadata.

mods.name: Keybinds Galore
mods.description: Keybind pie menu / QoL mod. Originally by Cael, updated by HVB007.

releases.notes:
Please head over to [Modrinth](https://modrinth.com/mod/keybindsgalore+(hvb007)/version/1.6.1) for more upto date and frequent releases.

### Fixes & Improvements

*   **Holding Down Keys Works Again:** Holding down a key with conflicts (like **Attack** or **Use Item**) now works continuously instead of just performing a single click.
*   **Ignored Keys Are Fixed:** Keys like **Space**, **Shift**, and **S** now work correctly again, even if they have conflicts.
*   **Middle Mouse Button Fixed:** The pie menu now closes properly when you release the middle mouse button.
*   **Better Conflict Warnings:** The warning message for prioritized keys (like "Attack") will now correctly show you what other keybinds are conflicting.
*   **Fixed Startup Crashes:** Solved several crashes and errors that happened on startup, especially when using transparent colors in the config file or running on newer Minecraft versions.
*   **Removed Reload Keybind:** The "Reload Config" keybind was causing startup crashes on some game versions, so it has been removed for now.
